fire.name: Fire & Explosion Response
fire.desc: Identify a fire, choose the right extinguisher, evacuate safely.
fire.brief: An electrical panel has caught fire in your work area. You will identify the hazard, pick the correct extinguisher, find a clear exit, complete the headcount and give the all-clear.
fire.debrief: You practised identifying a fire hazard, selecting CO₂ for an electrical fire, choosing an unblocked exit, running an evacuation headcount in order, and signalling all-clear to your supervisor.

s1.title: Step 1 · Identify the hazard
s1.prompt: Look around. Tap the fire hazard as soon as you see it.
s1.wrong: That is not the hazard. Look for flames or smoke — here, the electrical panel is burning.
s1.ok: Correct. The electrical panel is on fire.

s2.title: Step 2 · Choose the extinguisher
s2.prompt: This is an electrical fire near a panel. Tap the correct extinguisher.
s2.wrong: Wrong choice. Water and foam conduct electricity and can electrocute you. Use CO₂ on electrical fires.
s2.ok: Correct. CO₂ is safe on live electrical equipment.

s3.title: Step 3 · Find the exit
s3.prompt: Follow the green arrows. Tap the exit that is actually clear.
s3.wrong: That route is blocked by debris. Never force a blocked exit — take the clear one.
s3.ok: Correct. That exit is clear and reachable.

s4.title: Step 4 · Evacuation headcount
s4.prompt: Tap the three evacuation steps in the correct order, top to bottom.
s4.wrong: Out of order. Reach the assembly point first, then count workers, then report anyone missing.

s5.title: Step 5 · All clear
s5.prompt: The area is safe. Tap ALL CLEAR to close the emergency.
s5.wrong: Not yet. Give the all-clear signal to end the emergency.
s5.ok: Well done. The emergency is closed.

gas.name: Gas Leak & Confined Space
gas.desc: Spot a leak, wear the right PPE, use the buddy system, escape upwind.
gas.brief: A gas leak has been reported near a confined vessel. You will locate the leak, select the correct PPE, set up the buddy system, evacuate upwind and raise the alarm for a collapsed worker.
gas.debrief: You practised locating a leaking joint, choosing SCBA and gas-rated gloves, assigning entrant and standby roles, evacuating upwind of the cloud, and — most importantly — raising the alarm instead of entering to rescue.

s1.title: Step 1 · Find the leak
s1.prompt: Gas is escaping somewhere on this pipe. Tap the source of the leak.
s1.wrong: That is not leaking. Look for the joint with escaping vapour around it.
s1.ok: Correct. The valve joint is leaking.

s2.title: Step 2 · Select your PPE
s2.prompt: Tap the two items you must wear before approaching: breathing protection and hand protection.
s2.wrong: That will not protect you. A dust mask does not stop toxic gas, and ear muffs are irrelevant here.
s2.ok: Correct. SCBA mask and gas-rated gloves.

s3.title: Step 3 · Buddy system
s3.prompt: Assign roles. Tap the worker who enters first, then the worker who stays outside.
s3.wrong: Wrong order. Tap the entrant first, then the standby who never enters the space.
s3.ok: Correct. One entrant inside, one standby outside at all times.

s4.title: Step 4 · Evacuate
s4.prompt: The cloud is drifting. Tap the exit that takes you upwind, away from the gas.
s4.wrong: That exit leads into the gas cloud. Always move upwind, across the wind if you must.
s4.ok: Correct. Upwind and clear of the cloud.

s5.title: Step 5 · Raise the alarm
s5.prompt: Your buddy has collapsed inside. Tap the correct action.
s5.wrong: Never enter to rescue. Most confined-space deaths are would-be rescuers. Raise the alarm and wait for trained rescuers with breathing apparatus.
s5.ok: Correct. Raise the alarm — trained rescuers with air supply go in, never you.
